requirement: PAM during offshore wind construction and operation may be required by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and Bureau of Ocean Energy Management through project-related permits and approvals issued pursuant to relevant statutes and regulations.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and Bureau of Ocean Energy Management permits and approvals pursuant to relevant statutes and regulations
related_domains: passive acoustic monitoring; environmental impact assessment; marine species protection

requirement: Project-specific PAM Plans, developed by project proponents and approved by Federal agencies, should include descriptions of equipment, procedures (deployment, retrieval, detection, and analyses), ISO data quality standards and protocols that will be used for monitoring and mitigation.
scope: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) plans for offshore wind projects
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; acoustic monitoring; data quality

requirement: PAM specifications for inclusion in a PAM Plan will need to be developed in consultation with NOAA and other permitting agencies, such as BOEM.
scope: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) plans for offshore wind projects
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; acoustic monitoring; permitting

requirement: To design a PAM Plan, the following six topics need to be included and addressed: species of interest, PAM system types, PAM recording technologies, PAM study design, PAM system requirements, and PAM data archiving and reporting.
scope: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) plans for offshore wind projects
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; acoustic monitoring; data management; reporting

requirement: Rules for defining which acoustic information triggers this decision [delaying, ceasing, or proceeding with pile driving when a protected species is confirmed acoustically within a relevant impact zone] should be established in advance and in concert with visual monitoring.
related_domains: marine mammal protection; acoustic impact mitigation; construction monitoring

requirement: A thorough decision-making and communication process when a detection [of a species] is made is needed to ensure that vessels are alerted and slow down.
scope: Vessel operations during construction and operation
related_domains: vessel strike mitigation; collision avoidance; marine mammal protection

requirement: Slow Zones are established when North Atlantic right whales are detected both visually (i.e., Dynamic Management Area) and acoustically (i.e., Acoustic Slow Zone).
scope: Areas where North Atlantic right whales are detected
related_domains: marine mammal protection; vessel speed restriction; environmental impact mitigation

requirement: A Dynamic Management Area is triggered when 3 or more North Atlantic right whales are sighted within 3–5 miles of one another.
scope: Areas where North Atlantic right whales are sighted
related_domains: marine mammal protection; vessel speed restriction; environmental impact mitigation

requirement: An Acoustic Slow Zone is established when three or more upcall detections from an acoustic system occur within an evaluation period (e.g., 15 min)
scope: Areas where North Atlantic right whale upcalls are acoustically detected
related_domains: marine mammal protection; vessel speed restriction; environmental impact mitigation

requirement: To trigger an Acoustic Slow Zone, an acoustic system must meet the following criteria: (1) evaluation of the system has been published in the peer-reviewed literature, (2) false detection rate is 10% or lower over daily time scales, and (3) missed detection rate is 50% or lower over daily time scales.
scope: Acoustic detection systems for North Atlantic right whales
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; marine mammal detection; data quality

requirement: Once triggered, Slow Zones are set up as a rectangular area encompassing a circle of 15 (for Dynamic Management Areas) or 20 (for Acoustic Slow Zones) nautical miles around the core sightings (Dynamic Management Area) or recorder location at the time of detection (Acoustic Slow Zone).
scope: Slow Zones for North Atlantic right whales
related_domains: vessel speed restriction; navigation; marine mammal protection

requirement: Once triggered, Slow Zones are set up as a rectangular area encompassing a circle of 15 (for Dynamic Management Areas) or 20 (for Acoustic Slow Zones) nautical miles around the core sightings (Dynamic Management Area) or recorder location at the time of detection (Acoustic Slow Zone).
scope: Slow Zones for North Atlantic right whales
related_domains: vessel speed restriction; navigation; marine mammal protection

requirement: The Slow Zone lasts for 15 days and can be extended with additional sightings or acoustic detections.
scope: Slow Zones for North Atlantic right whales
related_domains: vessel speed restriction; navigation; marine mammal protection

requirement: The hydrophones and related hardware need to be calibrated (every 3 to 5 years) and their performance systematically measured and optimized within frequency bandwidths of interest for the particular activity, species, and environment.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; environmental monitoring

requirement: Calibration data, and relevant settings and sensitivities should be noted for all hardware used in recording/monitoring to ensure consistency among measurements for particular hardware and software.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; data management

requirement: Array synchronization information (where relevant) should also be documented.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; data management

requirement: This information should be permanently associated with the recordings as metadata.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring; data management

requirement: All hardware should be tested and optimized for low self-noise, including the mooring system.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring

requirement: In addition to calibration, the system should be fully tested to ensure adequate sensitivity in the area where it will be deployed and with the type of signals it would receive.
related_domains: acoustic monitoring

requirement: If this cannot be done at the project site, the system should be fully tested in a comparable location (i.e., an area exhibiting similar depth, temperature, substrate, current, acoustic propagation, and ambient noise, with relevant sound sources).

requirement: When real-time PAM is used during construction for mitigation purposes, a subset of the information required on species detections is expected to be provided and uploaded no later than 24 after the detection.

requirement: When PAM is used for long-term monitoring, all data (detection data, metadata, GPS data, and ambient noise data) should be provided via the formatted spreadsheets and uploaded within 90 days of the retrieval of the recorder or data collection.
